code.title: Add Two Numbers Function
code.description:
Modular programs start with tiny reusable units. Define a function int add(int a, int b) that receives two integers as parameters and returns their sum. Read the two integers in main and print the result by calling the function.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b.

Output Format:
Sum: <a + b>

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000

code.title: Circle Area Function Drill
code.description:
A drafting office needs circle areas all day long. Define a function double areaOfCircle(double radius) that receives the radius as a parameter and returns the area computed with PI = 3.14159. Read the radius (a double) in main and print the radius and the area (two decimal places) returned by the function.

Input Format:
One line with one double: radius.

Output Format:
Radius: <radius>
Area: <PI * r * r with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0.1 <= radius <= 1000

code.title: Even Checker Function
code.description:
A parity test is a classic one-line function. Define bool isEven(int n) that returns true when n is divisible by 2 and false otherwise. Read an integer in main and print the number together with the boolean result returned by the function.

Input Format:
One line with one integer n.

Output Format:
Number: <n>
Even: <true or false>

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000

code.title: Grade From Marks Function
code.description:
An exam cell assigns letter grades through a small pure function. Define char gradeFrom(int marks) that returns 'A' for marks 90 or above, 'B' for 75 to 89, 'C' for 60 to 74, 'D' for 40 to 59 and 'F' below 40. Read the marks in main and print them with the grade returned by the function.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: marks.

Output Format:
Marks: <marks>
Grade: <letter>

Constraints:
0 <= marks <= 100

code.title: Max of Three Function
code.description:
Finding the largest of three values is a natural fit for a function with three parameters. Define int maxOfThree(int a, int b, int c); the arguments are passed by value, so the function works on copies of the caller's data and returns the largest of them. Read three integers in main and print the maximum returned by the function.

Input Format:
One line with three integers a, b and c.

Output Format:
Max: <largest of the three>

Constraints:
-100000 <= each value <= 100000

code.title: Line Printer Function
code.description:
Decorative separators are printed over and over, so they belong in a reusable void function. Define void printLine(int n) that prints n hyphen characters '-' on one line followed by a newline. It takes no result back, so its return type is void. Read n in main, call the function, then print the word END on the next line.

Input Format:
One line with one integer n.

Output Format:
A line containing exactly n hyphens, then a second line containing END.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 30

code.title: Photocopy Shop Bill Function
code.description:
A photocopy shop charges a fixed rate per page and wants the billing logic isolated in one function. Write int billFor(int copies, int ratePerPage) that receives both values as parameters and returns copies * ratePerPage. Read the number of copies and the rate in main and print the bill using the function's return value.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: copies and rate per page.

Output Format:
Copies: <copies>
Rate: <rate>
Bill: <copies * rate>

Constraints:
1 <= copies <= 500, 1 <= rate <= 50

code.title: Travel Time Function
code.description:
A logistics app estimates trip duration from distance and speed. Define double hoursFor(double distance, double speed) that returns distance / speed. Read the distance in km and the average speed in km/h in main, then print both values and the hours returned by the function with exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with two doubles: distance and speed.

Output Format:
Distance: <distance>
Speed: <speed>
Hours: <distance / speed with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= distance <= 5000, 0 < speed <= 300

code.title: Password Strength Label Function
code.description:
A signup form labels every password the user types. Define string strengthLabel(string pw) that receives the password as a parameter and returns STRONG when its length is at least 12, MEDIUM when its length is at least 8, and WEAK otherwise. Read the password (a single word without spaces) in main and print it with the label returned by the function.

Input Format:
One line with one word: the password (no spaces).

Output Format:
Password: <pw>
Strength: <STRONG or MEDIUM or WEAK>

Constraints:
1 <= length of pw <= 30

code.title: Tip Splitter Function
code.description:
After a team lunch one person pays the tip and everyone shares it equally. Define double shareOf(double tipAmount, int friends) that returns tipAmount / friends. Read the tip amount (a double) and the number of friends (an integer) in main, then print the tip, the friend count and the per-friend share (two decimal places) using the function.

Input Format:
One line with a double and an integer: tip amount and friend count.

Output Format:
Tip: <tip, 2 decimals>
Friends: <friends>
Per friend: <tip / friends, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= tip <= 100000, 1 <= friends <= 20

code.title: Reference Swap Helper
code.description:
Call by reference gives a function real power over the caller's variables. Read two integers, print them, then call void swapVals(int& a, int& b) which exchanges the two integers through reference parameters. Print the values again after the call to show that the change survived outside the function.

Input Format:
One line with two integers x and y.

Output Format:
Before: <x> <y>
After: <y> <x>

Constraints:
-100000 <= x, y <= 100000

code.title: Pointer Counter Bump
code.description:
A footfall counter at a door is incremented through its address. Define void bump(int* counter) that receives a pointer and adds 1 to the pointed-to value using *counter. Read the starting count in main and call bump three times with &count, printing the count after every call and the final value.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: starting count.

Output Format:
Start: <count>
After bump 1: <count + 1>
After bump 2: <count + 2>
After bump 3: <count + 3>
Final: <count + 3>

Constraints:
-1000000 <= starting count <= 1000000

code.title: Overloaded Temperature Convert Suite
code.description:
A weather service exposes one convert operation for two kinds of data, so the function is overloaded:
- int convert(int celsius) computes Fahrenheit using whole-number arithmetic: (celsius * 9) / 5 + 32 with integer division
- double convert(double celsius) computes celsius * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0 exactly
Read one integer Celsius reading and one double Celsius reading, then print both conversions. The compiler picks the right overload automatically from the argument type.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: an integer Celsius value and a double Celsius value.

Output Format:
Rounded: <int convert result> F
Exact: <double convert result with 2 decimals> F

Constraints:
-100 <= each Celsius value <= 100

code.title: Discount Engine Default Argument
code.description:
Festival season prices carry a standard 5 percent discount, but special sales pass their own percentage. Define double discountedPrice(double price, int percent = 5) with a default argument for the percent parameter. In main, read the price and one special percentage, then call the function twice: once with only the price (so the default 5 percent applies) and once with the special percentage. Input Format: One line with a double and an integer: price and special discount percent. Output Format: Price: With 5% discount: With

% discount: Constraints: 1 <= price <= 100000, 0 <= special percent <= 90

code.title: Min Max via Reference Out Params
code.description:
A statistics helper reports two results at once, so it fills them through reference out-parameters instead of return values. Define void findMinMax(int a, int b, int c, int& mn, int& mx) that stores the smallest of the three values in mn and the largest in mx. Read three integers in main, call the helper and print the results after the call.

Input Format:
One line with three integers a, b and c.

Output Format:
Min: <smallest>
Max: <largest>

Constraints:
-100000 <= each value <= 100000

code.title: Modular Billing Pipeline
code.description:
A stationery vendor's billing runs as a pipeline of small cooperating functions:
- int subtotal(int rate, int quantity) returns rate * quantity
- double withTax(double amount, int taxPercent) returns amount + amount * taxPercent / 100.0
Read the unit rate, the quantity and the tax percent in main, then print the subtotal and the tax-inclusive grand total using the two functions.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: unit rate, quantity and tax percent.

Output Format:
Subtotal: <rate * quantity>
Tax: <tax amount, 2 decimals>
Grand total: <subtotal + tax, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= rate <= 5000, 1 <= quantity <= 1000, 0 <= tax percent <= 40

code.title: Expense Report Engine
code.description:
An expense-report tool is built from cooperating functions:
- void readExpense(string& label, double& amount) parses one expense through reference parameters
- double totalOf(double a, double b) returns the sum of two amounts
- void swapByRef(double& x, double& y) swaps through references
- void swapByPtr(double* x, double* y) swaps through pointers
Read two expenses (a single-word label and a double amount each). Print the report with the total, then swap the two amounts by reference and print, then swap them back by pointer and print.

Input Format:
One line with four tokens: label1, amount1, label2, amount2.

Output Format:
=== EXPENSE REPORT ===
<label1>: <amount1, 2 decimals>
<label2>: <amount2, 2 decimals>
Total: <sum, 2 decimals>
After reference swap:
<label1>: <amount2, 2 decimals>
<label2>: <amount1, 2 decimals>
After pointer swap:
<label1>: <amount1, 2 decimals>
<label2>: <amount2, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0.01 <= each amount <= 1000000

code.title: Cloud Storage Ladder Function
code.description:
A cloud storage plan prices data in a ladder, and the finance team needs each slab's cost separately, so the function fills its results through reference out-parameters. Define void computeLadder(int gb, double& slab1, double& slab2, double& slab3, double& total) where:
- the first 50 GB cost 2.50 per GB
- the next 100 GB (51 to 150) cost 4.00 per GB
- every GB above 150 costs 6.00 per GB
The function fills slab1, slab2 and slab3 with each slab's cost and total with their sum. Read the data used (integer GB) and print the full ladder.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: GB used.

Output Format:
Data: <gb> GB
Slab 1 (first 50): <cost, 2 decimals>
Slab 2 (next 100): <cost, 2 decimals>
Slab 3 (above 150): <cost, 2 decimals>
Total: <total, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 <= gb <= 10000

code.title: Bank Transaction Classifier
code.description:
A bank teller terminal classifies each transaction and computes fees through one function. Define void classify(char type, double amount, string& label, double* fee) that sets label to Deposit for 'D' or Withdrawal for 'W' through the reference parameter, and stores the fee through the pointer: withdrawals of 10000.00 or more carry a fee of 0.5 percent of the amount, all other transactions are free. Read two transactions (type and amount each), classify both and print a receipt with the total fees.

Input Format:
One line with four tokens: type1 (D or W), amount1, type2 (D or W), amount2.

Output Format:
TXN 1: <label> of <amount, 2 decimals> (Fee: <fee, 2 decimals>)
TXN 2: <label> of <amount, 2 decimals> (Fee: <fee, 2 decimals>)
Total fees: <sum of fees, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= each amount <= 1000000, type is D or W

code.title: Payroll Function Suite
code.description:
Month-end payroll runs as a suite of cooperating functions:
- double grossSalary(double basic, double bonusPercent = 10) returns basic plus bonusPercent percent of basic (the default bonus is 10 percent)
- double totalDeductions(double gross) returns 12 percent of gross
- double netSalary(double gross, double deductions) returns gross minus deductions
- void printSlip(string name, double net) prints one employee's slip
- void printSlip(string name, double net, double bonusAmount) is an overloaded variant that also prints the bonus amount
Read employee 1 (name and basic) and employee 2 (name, basic and an integer bonus percent). Process employee 1 with the default bonus using the two-parameter print overload; process employee 2 with the given bonus using the three-parameter print overload.

Input Format:
One line with five tokens: name1 (single word), basic1 (double), name2 (single word), basic2 (double), bonus2 (integer percent).

Output Format:
Employee: <name1>
Net pay: <net1, 2 decimals>
Employee: <name2>
Bonus: <bonus amount, 2 decimals>
Net pay: <net2, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1000 <= each basic <= 500000, 0 <= bonus2 <= 50

mcqs.title: Function Prototype Purpose
mcqs.description: In C++, what does a function declaration (prototype) such as int add(int a, int b); tell the compiler?
mcqs.Option1: The function's name, return type and parameter types, so the function can be called before its definition appears
mcqs.Option2: The complete body of the function
mcqs.Option3: The memory address where the function's local variables will be stored
mcqs.Option4: That the function cannot return any value

mcqs.title: Purpose of a Return Type
mcqs.description: What does the return type written before a function's name specify?
mcqs.Option1: How many parameters the function accepts
mcqs.Option2: The name of the variable that receives the result
mcqs.Option3: The type of the value the function sends back to the caller
mcqs.Option4: Whether the function runs in a loop

mcqs.title: Meaning of void Return Type
mcqs.description: A function is declared as void printReport(). What does void indicate?
mcqs.Option2: The function returns no value to the caller
mcqs.Option4: The function cannot be called from main

mcqs.title: Why Split Programs into Functions
mcqs.description: Which statement best explains how functions support modular programming?
mcqs.Option1: They make the program compile slower but safer
mcqs.Option2: They force every variable to become global
mcqs.Option3: They remove the need for the main function
mcqs.Option4: They break a big task into smaller named units that can be written, tested and reused independently

mcqs.title: Scope of Variables Inside a Function
mcqs.description: A variable declared inside a function body (a local variable) is:
mcqs.Option1: Visible to every function in the program
mcqs.Option4: Local to that function and destroyed when the function ends

mcqs.title: Parameter vs Argument
mcqs.description: In the call int s = add(x, y); what are x and y called, and what are a and b in the definition int add(int a, int b)?
mcqs.Option1: x and y are parameters; a and b are arguments
mcqs.Option3: x and y are arguments in the call; a and b are parameters in the definition

mcqs.title: What the return Statement Does
mcqs.description: What happens when a return statement executes inside a function?
mcqs.Option1: The function restarts from its first line
mcqs.Option2: The whole program exits immediately in every case
mcqs.Option3: The function stops and sends the value back to the caller at the point of the call
mcqs.Option4: The value is printed on screen automatically

mcqs.title: Flow of a Function Call
mcqs.description: When main calls a function, what is the order of control flow?
mcqs.Option1: The function body runs before main starts
mcqs.Option2: Control jumps to the function, its body runs, then control returns to the statement after the call
mcqs.Option3: Both main and the function run at the same time
mcqs.Option4: Control jumps to the function and never comes back

mcqs.title: Matching Arguments to Parameters
mcqs.description: A function is declared as int maxOfThree(int a, int b, int c). Which call supplies arguments that match the parameter list correctly?

mcqs.title: Return Type Must Match Usage
mcqs.description: double areaOfCircle(double r) returns a double. Which statement is true about the call double a = areaOfCircle(2.5);?
mcqs.Option1: The call is illegal because functions cannot return doubles
mcqs.Option2: The value is returned only if cout is used inside the function
mcqs.Option3: a receives the address of the function
mcqs.Option4: The returned double value is stored in a

mcqs.description: What does this program print?

mcqs.description: What does this program print?

mcqs.description: What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Copies in Call by Value
mcqs.description: When a function receives an argument by value, what does it actually work with?
mcqs.Option1: A reference bound to the caller's variable
mcqs.Option2: The memory address of the caller's variable
mcqs.Option3: A separate copy of the argument's value, so changes inside the function never affect the caller
mcqs.Option4: The caller's variable itself under a new name

mcqs.title: Declare Before Use
mcqs.description: A helper function is defined below main in the same file and main calls it above the definition, with no prototype anywhere. What happens at compile time?
mcqs.Option1: The compiler scans the whole file first, so it compiles without any declaration
mcqs.Option2: The function is automatically treated as returning void
mcqs.Option3: The call is skipped silently at runtime
mcqs.Option4: The compiler reports an error because the function is used before it is declared

mcqs.description: Passing a char into these two overloads follows well-defined promotion rules. What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Reference Parameter Accumulates
mcqs.description: The same reference parameter is modified by two calls. What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Reference and Pointer Out-Params Together
mcqs.description: One function writes results through a reference parameter and a pointer parameter. What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Rightmost Rule for Default Arguments
mcqs.description: Which rule about default arguments in C++ is correct?
mcqs.Option1: They may be given only to the rightmost parameters; once one parameter has a default, every parameter to its right must also have one
mcqs.Option2: They may be given to any single parameter, even the leftmost one alone
mcqs.Option3: They are permitted only inside void functions
mcqs.Option4: They change the function's return type to the type of the default value
